text:
alex.g: seeing a nasty pattern in us-east1-gpu during the last 12m — big load spike and the autoscaler is slow to actually provision nodes, then it launches several at once and we get thrash + failed scheduling. pods are Pending for minutes. anyone else?
maria.sre: yep alerted. metrics show nodepool create latency spiking to ~4m and then a flurry of node joins which coincides with kube-scheduler backpressure. suspect control-plane rate limits on the cloud side.
sre-bot: [ALERT] autoscaler_high_sync_lag us-east1-gpu detected 1917554327 — 4m avg node provision latency, pending pods > 120
devon.infra: checking cloud console now. api error 429s during provisioning window. looks like quota/soft-throttle on the provider side for GPU instance creations in the AZ.
lee.runtime: traffic shift is failing too — the fallback routing rule didn't kick because the service health probe saw nodes but pods never scheduled. frontend 502s for a subset of requests.
alex.g: repro: run `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep Pending | wc -l` shows 137 pending. scheduler events: `0/12 nodes are available: Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu` even though nodes are being created.
maria.sre: that's the classic race: nodes land but tainted or missing GPU plugin init -> pods pending for init containers, then we slam the autoscaler again. can we pause new traffic to the affected pool?
devon.infra: temporarily routed new jobs to us-west1 via the proxy header rule. I pushed a manual override to the router: `route: inference -> us-west1 (weight 100)`. watching cost/backpressure.
lee.runtime: rolling out a lightweight sidecar fix to skip the GPU-plugin init for warm nodes — will try to speed scheduling for in-flight pods. patch id `pr/5883`.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: started rollout pr/5883 to inference-deploy (canary 10%).
alex.g: also seeing a ton of short-lived node churn — node join -> kubelet crash -> re-register loop. cloud logs show driver install timeout on some instance images.
maria.sre: action list: 1) pause autoscaler scale ups (devon can flip the flag) 2) route traffic to west 3) blacklist problem image family 4) escalate quota to cloud support.
devon.infra: paused autoscaler at 1917554380 via config `autoscaler.scale_up_enabled=false` and set cold-pool buffer to 0. routing weight to us-west1 is in effect.
lee.runtime: canary patch is green on 10% after 2m. promoting to 50% to clear pending pods faster.
alex.g: also opening a billing watch — this could spike GPU spend if we keep thrashing. started alert to FinOps channel.
maria.sre: good. i'll collect events and prepare a short postmortem stub. need timestamps for the spike window: start ~1917554270, mitigation begin ~1917554380.
devon.infra: cloud support ticket created: TKT-98734, mentioned soft-throttling and driver bootstrap failures.
lee.runtime: tip — for pending pods you can force-schedule by deleting the problematic init container config, but doing that is risky. i'm going to drain one problematic node to reproduce locally.
alex.g: timeline note: primary failure mode = provider-side creation throttles + image/driver bootstrap timeouts -> autoscaler overcompensates -> scheduling thrash -> traffic fallthrough and increased 5xx.
sre-bot: [INFO] incident create: incident/2026-03-18-autoscale-thrash-east created by maria.sre at 1917554460
maria.sre: running playbook: notify oncall, set incident channel, collect `kubectl describe node` samples, and snapshot autoscaler logs. will post short runbook in #incidents.
devon.infra: pushing a temporary change to prefer preemptibleless node flavor to avoid quota domain that is being throttled. will monitor.
lee.runtime: pods are draining from pending into running after canary increase — pending count down to 18.
alex.g: good progress. once stable let's slowly shift traffic back and unpause autoscaler, but keep a tighter cooldown and lower max surge.
maria.sre: agreed. post-incident followups: validate node image bake, add autoscaler hysteresis + backoff on 429s, add cloud quota guardrails.
sre-bot: [RESOLVED] autoscaler_high_sync_lag cleared at 1917554990 — metrics normalized, pending pods < 5.
